profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading:
This building operates as Equinix's DC21 data center at 22175 Beaumeade Circle, Ashburn, Virginia, on a different street than the Performance Circle and Uunet Way buildings covered elsewhere in this campus grouping, inside Loudoun County's Data Center Alley. Equinix's own DC21 facility page lists this as a two story building with a precast concrete exterior, structural steel frame, and slab on grade construction, totaling 39,665 square feet (3,685 square meters), the smallest of the four DC numbered buildings covered in this research pass. The page publishes N+2 UPS redundancy, higher than the N+1 figure listed for several nearby Equinix buildings, alongside N+1 generator redundancy rated for 30 hours or more of runtime at full load, 240v/415v power distribution, and a minimum cabinet density of 5kVA. Cooling redundancy is listed as N+2, floor load capacity at 250 pounds per square foot, and fire suppression as double interlock pre-action. Security is listed as 24/7 with biometric entrance mantraps and video recording surveillance, and building amenities listed include a breakroom, conference rooms, showers, and WiFi. Equinix lists nine certifications for DC21, HECVAT, HIPAA, ISO 22301, ISO 27001, ISO 9001, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, and SOC 2 Type II, plus a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment. DC21's page is also the only one among the four buildings in this pass to name a renewable energy source directly, wind power purchase agreements sourced from Texas and Oklahoma. Equinix does not publish an IT load or utility power figure in megawatts for DC21 itself, so this entry does not assign one.

Ashburn's Data Center Alley predates Equinix's arrival. AOL built what is generally regarded as the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support its dial up internet subscriber base, and the fiber capacity that project attracted into Loudoun County helped seed the interconnected cluster that followed, including Virginia's early MAE East internet exchange. Equinix opened its first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and its second, DC2, earned a reputation, per Data Center Dynamics, as one of the most connected buildings on earth. Data Center Dynamics describes the resulting corridor as roughly 10 million square feet of built data center space region wide, consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of electrical power across all operators combined, not Equinix alone.

Equinix's own Washington D.C. metro listing page currently names and links 15 facilities together, DC1 through DC6, DC10 through DC16, DC21, and DC22, with most addresses in Ashburn and at least one, DC14, in nearby Manassas. Equinix does not publish a combined power or square footage total for that group, and at least one building number appearing in public address records for the area, DC17, has no active linked page on Equinix's own site at present. Equinix markets its Ashburn buildings collectively as offering access to one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, along with Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products, without singling out DC21's own peering density or customer roster.

reading.body:
Equinix DC21 is a 39,665 square foot facility on Equinix's Ashburn campus in Loudoun County, Virginia, part of Data Center Alley. The operator publishes no power capacity, square footage density, or specific certifications for this building. DC2, described as representative of the campus's general specifications, offers N+1 power and cooling redundancy with a stated minimum cabinet density of 4 kVA, but these figures are not confirmed for DC21 itself.

Ashburn hosts the greatest published concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet, anchored by AOL's 1997 Dulles Technology Center and Equinix's DC1 and DC2 from the late 1990s. The region serves one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast. Virginia as a state has 330 mapped data center facilities and 23 with published power capacity totaling 1,375 megawatts.

Without published megawatt capacity, DC21 cannot be ranked by power among Virginia's 23 disclosed facilities or evaluated for its contribution to AI scaling capacity. The building's role in the Ashburn campus, historically positioned as an internet exchange hub rather than a compute facility, and the absence of any published specifications for this specific site, mean its relevance to AI infrastructure depends on information Equinix has not disclosed.
